notes: Use-case: customer product team (mid-market SaaS) — in-app conversational assistant + context search for docs and release notes.
Primary goal: migrate from hosted proof-of-concept to Dedicated to reduce per-token costs and guarantee throughput for peak events.
Targets: p95 latency <=150ms for short-chat (<=512 tokens); sustained throughput ~250 req/s; spikes up to 800rps for brief window.
Cost sensitivity: high — wants recommendations for batching/quantization; target ARR savings 40% vs hosted at scale.
Model preference: open models with 8-bit quantization first; fallback to a higher-capacity variant for edge cases.
Routing/POC requirements: canary rollout sequence 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated rollback on QoR regressions; cross-region failover to hosted fallback in us-east if dedicated region degraded.
Canary plan details requested: traffic split automation, metrics to watch (latency p50/p95, error rate, token cost), rollback triggers (>=20% latency increase or >=3x error rate).
"We need deterministic performance during release week — can't risk >200ms p95," said Head of Product (K. Morales).
Security asks: SSO (SAML), SOC2 evidence, KMS integration for customer keys, data residency options (US-only preferred).
POC scope: 2-week functional verification + 4-week load validation on Dedicated; initial canary in us-west then expand.
Internal blockers: finance needs committed pricing; infra team needs firewall rules and VPC peering; SE to supply infra checklist by 2024-11-06.
Action items: Jordan to share Dedicated POC SOW; Evan to coordinate security artifact delivery; customer to confirm test dataset by 2024-11-07.
use_case_summary: Mid-market SaaS product team evaluating hosted -> dedicated. POC focused on canary deployments, fallback routing to hosted, model variants for cost/quality tradeoffs, and cross-region failover. Success: stable p95 latency <=150ms and 40% cost reduction at scale.
